question: In close Spanish league games, when did referees add the most stoppage time at the end?
options: When the home side trailed by one
When the home side led by one
answer: When the home side trailed by one. Garicano, Palacios-Huerta and Prendergast found referees added roughly twice as much time when it could help the home team as when it could hurt it, and the bias grew with the crowd. Nobody was bribed: the referee was quietly giving the stands what they wanted.
move: Small judgement calls are where social pressure hides most easily.
ask: Where do I give extra time or slack to the people who happen to be watching me?
trap: Assuming timekeeping is too mechanical to bend toward the crowd.
source: Garicano et al., Rev Econ Stat, 2005
reference: Garicano, Palacios-Huerta & Prendergast, Favoritism Under Social Pressure, Review of Economics and Statistics, 2005
